seo.title: American Express: deep learning fraud detection - +6% accuracy, lowest fraud rate (2021)
seo.meta_description: Amex scores every transaction in milliseconds across ~$1.2T in annual spend. Deep learning on GPU improved detection accuracy by 6%.
seo.resume_citable: American Express scores every transaction in milliseconds across roughly $1.2 trillion in annual spend; the move to deep learning on GPU improved fraud detection accuracy by 6%, and the network claims the lowest fraud rate in the industry for 14 consecutive years (Nilson, 2021).

faq.q: How does American Express detect fraud?
faq.a: Machine learning and deep learning models evaluate every transaction at the moment of authorization, compare it to the cardholder's spending habits, and return a decision in milliseconds, across the entire global network.

faq.q: What gain did deep learning deliver?
faq.a: Served on GPU via NVIDIA TensorRT and Triton, it improved fraud detection accuracy by 6% over the previous models.

pattern: real-time fraud detection with deep learning
objectif_business: Detect fraud on every transaction in milliseconds to limit losses and protect the customer relationship, while keeping the false-decline rate low enough not to block legitimate purchases.
description: American Express runs machine learning models that evaluate every transaction at the moment of authorization, worldwide, and return a fraud decision in milliseconds. The models learn from the cardholder's spending habits and buying behavior at merchants. American Express monitors on the order of $1.2 trillion in annual spend and evaluates several billion transactions per year. By moving to deep learning models served on GPU (via NVIDIA TensorRT and Triton), fraud detection accuracy improved by 6%. The company claims the lowest fraud rate among the major card networks for 14 consecutive years, per the February 2021 Nilson Report.

resultats.metrique: Fraud detection accuracy improvement (move to deep learning on GPU)
Lowest fraud rate in the industry (Nilson Report, Feb. 2021)
Annual spend monitored in real time

niveau_preuve.justification: Figures documented by NVIDIA's technical blog (infrastructure partner, interested source) for the +6%, and by a specialist analysis (Emerj) that reports the monitored spend and the lowest-fraud-rate claim (from the Nilson Report cited by American Express). No financial result isolating the effect of AI.

stack_technique.detail: In-house models trained on cardholder spending habits and merchant context; fraud decision returned in milliseconds on each authorization.
Inference optimization for deep learning models on GPU, associated with the documented 6% accuracy gain.
Low-latency model serving in production on the global authorization stream.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Real time, on every authorization, with periodic retraining on confirmed fraud.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: AmEx AI Labs and American Express risk teams.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The cardholder's spending habits and confirmed-fraud labels. If labels arrive too late or are noisy, the model drifts and either lets fraud through or multiplies false declines.

etapes.detail: A transaction reaches authorization on the American Express network.
The deep learning models compare the transaction to the cardholder's habits and merchant context and return a score.
The transaction is approved, declined, or flagged for review depending on the score and thresholds.
Confirmed fraud and disputes flow back to feed retraining.

stack_possible: GPU inference for real-time deep learning
replication.premiere_etape: Assemble a set of labeled confirmed fraud and train a first scoring model on the highest-risk transactions.

playbook.action: Consolidate the transaction history with confirmed-fraud labels and per-cardholder spending profiles.
Train a first scoring model on the highest-risk transactions and evaluate it offline against the current rules.
playbook.livrable: Model evaluated (accuracy, false positives) against the baseline.

playbook.action: Connect the model in shadow mode on the authorization stream, with no customer impact, to check latency and scores under real conditions.
playbook.livrable: Shadow-mode report: production scores vs current decisions.

playbook.action: Move the model to decisioning on a limited segment, with thresholds, human review of ambiguous cases, and a dispute procedure.
playbook.livrable: Model in production on a defined scope, governance of the automated decision in place.

playbook.action: Build the retraining loop on confirmed fraud and disputes, with model drift monitoring.
playbook.livrable: Retraining pipeline and fraud / false-decline dashboard.

replication.equipe: 2-3 data scientists + 1 ML engineer (low-latency inference) + the risk/fraud team for thresholds and case review.

statut_vivant.note: ML fraud detection is a core American Express asset, operated by a dedicated AI Labs team. The pattern remains in production; the lowest-fraud-rate claim rests on a 2021 Nilson ranking, to be refreshed.

transposable_ue.note: Real-time fraud scoring applies to the network, the EU included. Under GDPR and the AI Act, the automated rejection of a transaction must remain supervisable and contestable; transaction data is processed on the legitimate-interest basis of fraud prevention.
